articles.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
articles.summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

articles.title: The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts, (Wed, Nov 4th)
articles.summary: One of the early web application vulnerabilities I remember was CVE-2000-0411 [CVE]. This was a simple vulnerability in a CGI-bin script used to send e-mail. The vulnerability was pretty straightforward: Adding additional parameters to the URL leaked environment variables. Other vulnerabilities allowed setting the "To" address and were heavily abused by spammers. And if parameters were passed directly to the sendmail binary, similar vulnerabilities could allow arbitrary code execution.

articles.title: Fake software installers are turning your PCs into profit centers for hackers
articles.summary:
Users looking for cracked commercial software, free games, plugins, and unofficial utilities could be signing up for more than a free download. Microsoft has observed an evolving campaign that uses trojanized installers to turn the downloading Windows devices into money-making machines, consuming their computing resources and internet bandwidth without informed consent.

articles.title: CrowdStrike launches AI kill switch to shut down rogue agents
articles.summary:
With a notable rise in autonomous AI agents veering off-script inside corporate networks, CrowdStrike has launched an enterprise AI Kill Switch, giving security teams control to cut off and disable models when they go rogue. 
Integrated into its Falcon Guardian platform, this AI Kill Switch will provide security teams with the human control to terminate the agent at its root, where it runs, block it from launching again, and even cut off its enterprise network access.

articles.summary:
CrowdStrike plans to acquire AI security companies Fiddler AI and Dreadnode in separate deals that will extend its Falcon platform into automated testing of AI systems and monitoring of AI agent behaviour, as enterprises look to address security risks arising from increasingly autonomous applications.

articles.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. articles.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

articles.title: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
articles.summary: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

articles.title: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
articles.summary: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's

articles.title: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.summary: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

articles.title: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.summary: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

clusters.summary: Organizations may not be ready for completely autonomous communication processes, but there are places where automating information updates would alleviate pressure.

clusters.title: The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts, (Wed, Nov 4th)
clusters.summary: One of the early web application vulnerabilities I remember was CVE-2000-0411 [CVE]. This was a simple vulnerability in a CGI-bin script used to send e-mail. The vulnerability was pretty straightforward: Adding additional parameters to the URL leaked environment variables. Other vulnerabilities allowed setting the "To" address and were heavily abused by spammers. And if parameters were passed directly to the sendmail binary, similar vulnerabilities could allow arbitrary code execution.

clusters.summary:
Users looking for cracked commercial software, free games, plugins, and unofficial utilities could be signing up for more than a free download. Microsoft has observed an evolving campaign that uses trojanized installers to turn the downloading Windows devices into money-making machines, consuming their computing resources and internet bandwidth without informed consent.

clusters.summary:
With a notable rise in autonomous AI agents veering off-script inside corporate networks, CrowdStrike has launched an enterprise AI Kill Switch, giving security teams control to cut off and disable models when they go rogue. 
Integrated into its Falcon Guardian platform, this AI Kill Switch will provide security teams with the human control to terminate the agent at its root, where it runs, block it from launching again, and even cut off its enterprise network access.

clusters.summary:
CrowdStrike plans to acquire AI security companies Fiddler AI and Dreadnode in separate deals that will extend its Falcon platform into automated testing of AI systems and monitoring of AI agent behaviour, as enterprises look to address security risks arising from increasingly autonomous applications.

It’s an idea that until recently would have been dismissed as absurd, yet across cybersecurity it’s now taken as a given.

clusters.title: Barracuda’s security appliances have a security problem of their own
clusters.summary:
Barracuda, which offers a wide variety of cybersecurity devices, has been bitten by a bug itself.
The company has disclosed two critical and high-severity vulnerabilities that, if chained together, could allow threat actors to bypass authorization controls and gain root access to devices.

clusters.title: Philippine Migrant Worker Data Likely Leaked in 69GB Government Breach
clusters.summary: An unknown operator appears to have exfiltrated SQL Server backups from the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration in under a half hour.

clusters.title: Phishing-Resistant Isn't Enough; Yubico Takes Aim at Identity-Verification Gap
clusters.summary: The new YubiID service bridges identity verification with credential enrollment and recovery across existing identity platforms, closing a phishing-resistant authentication gap. Plus: post-quantum YubiKey beta.

clusters.title: Fresh European Fridge Attacks Put Cold-Chain Security in Focus
clusters.summary: Beyond food storage, the same combination of Internet connectivity, remote access, and inadequate security practices can put temperature-controlled infrastructure across other critical sectors at risk.

clusters.title: Germany Busts 'Crime-as-a-Service' Investment Fraud Outfit
clusters.summary: Authorities seized more than 100 servers and arrested seven as part of a crackdown on a fraud network spanning more than 50 countries.

clusters.title: LLMjacking Emerges as Thriving Cybercriminal Enterprise
clusters.summary: Cybercriminals have turned reselling cloud access to LLMs into a lucrative business model, with some victims paying as much as $1 million in resource consumption before access was revoked.

clusters.summary: Evidence suggests a model may have generated and revised commands during the ransom gang's breach, though researchers stopped short of claiming full automation.

clusters.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. clusters.summary: Wireshark Release Candidate 5.0.0 was published: soon we can expect a new major version of Wireshark.

clusters.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
clusters.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

clusters.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
clusters.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

clusters.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
clusters.summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

clusters.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
clusters.summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

clusters.title: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
clusters.summary: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

clusters.title: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
clusters.summary: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. clusters.title: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
clusters.summary: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. In the days immediately following the suspect's arrest, remaining ShinyHunters members dramatically escalated their attacks, stealing highly sensitive data from the FBI and extorting the Russian ransomware group Cl0p.

clusters.title: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
clusters.summary: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

I suspect this is for CVE-2023-20198.

top3.summary:

The exploit lets anyone who can reach a switch's web management interface run commands on it without logging in. Zyxel has released new firmware for 10 GS1900 models that closes the hole.
